title: PR-thread-annotator-and-refactor-hypotheses
content:
Notes to self - quick brain dump (late-night)

Goal: capture signal from messy PR threads so follow-ups + refactors are actionable. Prototype ideas and a short checklist to use when eyeballing changes to serving-runtime, routing, or cache layers.

Why: too many PRs get merged with subtle performance regressions that only show up under tail latency. If we annotate the thread with likely failure modes and a minimal test matrix, reviewers can make faster, higher-quality calls.

High-level concept:
- PR-thread-annotator: a tiny bot/CLI that scans the PR + comments and emits a short annotation block to paste into the PR description or as a review comment.
  - Inputs: files changed, diff hunks, touched packages (serving-runtime, kv-cache, scheduler), CI results, comment keywords (perf, latency, regression, kv, cache, eviction)
  - Outputs (short): probable impact (latency/cost/functional), quick test suggestions, rollout advice, owner/SME hints

Annotation template (one-paragraph for reviewers):
- Impact: [latency/cost/functionality] (likely/hypothesis)
- Hot paths: list probable hotspots (e.g., kv_cache.py:put, router/route_selector.py line 230)
- Quick tests: 1) unit test to assert no regression in cache hit ratio under synthetic sequence 2) perf test on 4x batch with seq_len=1024 3) smoke on staging dedicated node type
- Rollout: canary percentage + fallback (do not enable quantization variant until verified)
- Signals to watch: tail P95/P99 latency, mem growth over 12h, error rate for reroute fallback

Checklist for manual review (short):
- [ ] Files touched include runtime-critical modules? (serving-runtime/core, runtime/execution_loop, kv-cache)
- [ ] New allocations per token? (look for list/dict per request in hot loops)
- [ ] Any change to batching boundaries or buffer sizes? if yes, ensure unit test + perf scenario
- [ ] Anything touching kernel selection or quantization paths? add model-level smoke
- [ ] New retry/backoff behavior that could multiply requests (watch duplicate enqueue)
- [ ] Config defaults changed? (if yes, ensure migration/feature-flag)
- [ ] Logging/metrics: do we have new metrics for the path? add at least one metric for regression detection
- [ ] Does the PR include a canary/rollback plan in the description? if not, ask for one

Refactor hypotheses (things we can do post-merge or enqueue):
- hypothesis A: decouple KV eviction policy from hot-path write path. If eviction triggers sync IO, move to background worker + admission control. Rationale: observed spikes when large batches hit full cache.
- hypothesis B: introduce a small 'allocation-pool' for transient token buffers allocated per-request in execution_loop to avoid churn in GC. Quick benchmark: run 10k requests with seq_len=512 and compare p99 with/without pool.
- hypothesis C: route-simplification: extract route selection heuristic into small pure function + unit tests so we can A/B test new heuristics without touching orchestrator state.

Quick measurement plan (minimal):
- Local perf harness: replay 2x production traces (use trace subset from customer X) through serving-runtime with PR branch and main; record P50/P95/P99, token throughput, mem usage.
- Staging smoke: run 30-min steady load on dedicated-small node using existing load generator (link: https://perf-tools/internal/replay/243) - check for leak or tail spikes.
- Post-merge: gated rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on >15% p99 increase or >0.5% error increase.

Unresolved questions (ask in PR as review comments):
- Why did change modify the retry window from 30ms -> 100ms? comment says "reduce thrash" but need data backing.
- The new cache code uses locks around put() - will this increase contention under batching? request author to add microbenchmark.
- There is a complex conditional in route_selector that looks duplicated from previous refactor (see lines 178-210) - can we dedupe and add unit tests for boundary inputs?

Possible quick patches to request before merge (low friction):
- Add one perf unit (python benchmark) that runs with seq_len=256 and batch sizes [1,4,16] and asserts p99 < baseline*1.08
- Add metric 'kv.put_block_time' and increment on slow-path to help triage
- Add a feature flag for the new retry policy (default off) so we can canary it quickly

Slack/Jira/PR links to drop in comments:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2134  (refer to the line comments about kv_cache)
- Perf harness: https://perf-tools/internal/replay/243
- Jira: JIRA-INF-482 (investigate cache eviction spike 2024-09-30)
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread ts=1623456789 (internal convo with @rina about batch contention)

Notes-to-self: when I prototype the annotator, keep it tiny: grep diffs for keywords, then heuristics mapping -> output templated block. MVP runbook: shell script + GitHub action that leaves a review comment. Later: extend with CI perf runs and small ML classifier for "high-risk" PRs.

Follow-ups (backlog):
- [ ] Prototype annotator CLI and GitHub Action (owner: jonah)
- [ ] Add perf unit tests to serving-runtime CI bucket 'micro-perf'
- [ ] Schedule 1:1 with Rina to review eviction policy refactor
- [ ] Write runbook for canary thresholds and rollback actions (SRE input required)

Rough time estimates:
- MVP annotator (script + GH action): 2-3 days
- Integrate perf harness + report: 1 week
- Add pool allocator refactor + benchmarks: 2-3 weeks

Random mental notes:
- avoid adding new global state without GC-friendly controls
- prefer feature flags for behavioral changes to allow quick rollback
- flag any PR touching 'kernel selection' or 'kv cache' as high risk in the annotator

End of dump. Will revisit after 1st prototype and drop into repo under tools/annotator/README.md
